questions.q: According to this lesson, why can't a Solidity-only developer ship a usable dApp?
options: A smart contract alone is useless to a normal user — the frontend, the libraries that talk to the chain, and the deploy/test scripts around it are all written in JavaScript or TypeScript
Solidity code cannot be deployed without first being rewritten in JavaScript
Smart contracts require no supporting code of any kind
JavaScript is required by Ethereum's protocol rules to validate any transaction
questions.explain: The contract is only one narrow piece — everything a user or developer actually touches around it is JavaScript/TypeScript.

questions.q: Which three places does this lesson say JavaScript shows up in a real dApp?
options: The frontend, the libraries that talk to the chain, and backend/scripts
Only inside the smart contract itself
Only in the wallet extension, nowhere else
Only on blockchain explorer websites
questions.explain: Frontend UI, chain-communication libraries like ethers.js/viem, and Node.js backend/scripts are the three places named.

questions.q: Why does this course spend two full chapters on plain JavaScript before introducing any blockchain library?
options: So fundamentals like const, arrow functions, async/await, and array methods are already second nature, instead of fighting unfamiliar syntax and an unfamiliar library at the same time
Because blockchain libraries cannot be taught at all
Because TypeScript is not used anywhere in this course
Because the course has no particular reason, it's just traditional ordering
questions.explain: Building JS fluency first removes one of the two things a beginner would otherwise have to learn simultaneously.

questions.q: Which two libraries does this lesson name as the dominant JavaScript/TypeScript libraries for talking to a blockchain?
options: ethers.js and viem
React and Next.js
Express and Fastify
jQuery and Lodash
questions.explain: ethers.js and viem are named as the two dominant libraries for reading chain data and sending transactions.

questions.q: What does the capstone in Chapter 7 of this course build, according to the roadmap in this lesson?
options: A typed Node/TypeScript script that reads real blockchain data
A full Solidity smart contract from scratch
A mobile app with no JavaScript involved
A Python data pipeline
questions.explain: The roadmap table lists the Chapter 7 capstone as a typed Node/TS script reading real blockchain data.
